contexts.label: Migraine-type headache features
contexts.description: Headache with features used by ICHD-3 migraine criteria (unilateral, pulsating, moderate/severe, aggravated by activity, nausea or photophobia+phonophobia). A context to consider — not a diagnosis; ICHD-3 also requires ≥5 attacks.

sources.reference: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (IHS, 2018)
NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

contexts.label: Tension-type headache features
contexts.description: Headache with ICHD-3 tension-type features (bilateral, pressing/tightening, mild–moderate, not aggravated by activity, no nausea). A context to consider — not a diagnosis.

sources.reference: International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (IHS, 2018)
NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

contexts.label: Dyspepsia / reflux symptoms
contexts.description: Upper-GI symptoms (heartburn, regurgitation, epigastric discomfort). Uninvestigated dyspepsia context per NICE CG184.

alarmFeatures.text: Age ≥ 55 with weight loss and upper-GI symptoms: consider urgent endoscopy/suspected-cancer pathway before empirical therapy (PPIs can mask symptoms).

sources.reference: NICE CG184 GORD and dyspepsia in adults
NICE NG12 Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
NICE CG184 GORD and dyspepsia in adults

contexts.label: Allergic rhinitis features
contexts.description: Sneezing, rhinorrhoea, nasal congestion and itchy eyes without fever.

sources.reference: Brożek JL et al. Allergic Rhinitis and its Impact on Asthma (ARIA) guidelines — 2016 revision. J Allergy Clin Immunol 2017

contexts.label: Acute undifferentiated fever
contexts.description: Fever of recent onset without a localising source in the entered data. In India, consider malaria/dengue/typhoid testing per local epidemiology and season.

alarmFeatures.text: Fever lasting more than 7 days warrants investigation for a cause before symptomatic treatment alone.

sources.reference: Clinical safety rule — prolonged fever
WHO/TDR Dengue guidelines (2009): avoid aspirin/NSAIDs

contexts.label: Acute upper respiratory infection (common cold) features
contexts.description: Runny nose, sore throat, cough and congestion of short duration. Usually viral and self-limiting.

sources.reference: ICMR Treatment Guidelines for Antimicrobial Use in Common Syndromes (2nd ed. 2019; revised 2022)
Kenealy T, Arroll B. Antibiotics for the common cold and acute purulent rhinitis. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2013

recommendations.statement: For acute migraine, combination therapy with an oral triptan and an NSAID, or an oral triptan and paracetamol, is recommended (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: Monotherapy with an oral triptan, NSAID, aspirin or paracetamol may be considered, taking patient preference and history into account (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: An anti-emetic may be considered in addition to acute migraine treatment, even without nausea or vomiting (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: Opioids and ergots are not recommended for acute migraine treatment (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: Aspirin, paracetamol or an NSAID may be considered for acute treatment of tension-type headache (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: Opioids are not recommended for acute tension-type headache (NICE CG150, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG150 Headaches in over 12s

recommendations.statement: For uninvestigated dyspepsia without alarm features, a full-dose PPI for 4 weeks (or H. pylori test-and-treat) is recommended; lifestyle review advised (NICE CG184, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE CG184 GORD and dyspepsia in adults

recommendations.statement: Oral second-generation H1-antihistamines or intranasal corticosteroids are recommended for allergic rhinitis (ARIA 2016, paraphrased). Intranasal corticosteroid records are not yet in this knowledge base.

sources.reference: Brożek JL et al. Allergic Rhinitis and its Impact on Asthma (ARIA) guidelines — 2016 revision. J Allergy Clin Immunol 2017

recommendations.statement: Paracetamol for symptomatic fever relief; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs where dengue has not been excluded (WHO 2009, paraphrased).

sources.reference: WHO/TDR Dengue guidelines (2009): avoid aspirin/NSAIDs

recommendations.statement: Paracetamol or ibuprofen may be advised for pain/fever in acute sore throat and common cold (NICE NG84, paraphrased).

sources.reference: NICE NG84 Sore throat (acute): antimicrobial prescribing

recommendations.statement: Antibiotics are not indicated for the common cold/viral upper respiratory infection (ICMR antimicrobial guidelines; Cochrane review 2013).

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.whatItIs: A widely used non-opioid pain reliever and fever reducer.
drugs.whatItDoes: Relieves mild-to-moderate pain and lowers fever. It has little anti-inflammatory effect.

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.pharmacologicClass: Salicylate NSAID; antiplatelet at low dose
drugs.whatItIs: A salicylate with analgesic, antipyretic and (at low dose) antiplatelet effects.
drugs.whatItDoes: Relieves pain and fever; at low doses it reduces platelet aggregation.
drugs.mechanism: Irreversible acetylation of cyclo-oxygenase (COX-1 > COX-2), reducing prostaglandin and thromboxane A2 synthesis.
